items.title: Parliament to debate new provinces next month, says minister
items.description:
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said on Thursday that parliament was expected to debate the issue of new provinces next month.
Addressing the corporate sector in late July, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had called for the creation of new provinces or administrative units, saying that the current system had “collapsed”.
“There is no National Assembly session this month; however, sessions of both the National Assembly and Senate are expected in October. The discussions will be held whenever the sessions are convened,” the minister said in a video statement.

items.title: Death toll from cargo ship fire in China rises to 25: state media
items.description:
The death toll from a fire that erupted on Thursday on a foreign-flagged cargo ship docked in a Chinese port has risen to 25, including five people who had been listed as missing, state media said.
The bulk carrier, moored in the eastern shipping hub of Qingdao, had 42 people on board when the fire broke out, according to state broadcaster CCTV.
17 of those were evacuated, including five who were injured.
However, by Thursday evening “all 25 missing persons had been found, none showing signs of life”, state broadcaster CCTV reported.
It said “the open flames were extinguished” by about 2:30 pm

items.description:

items.title: Islamabad extends rare greeting to Pyongyang
items.description:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan on Wed­nesday made an unusual public diplomatic gesture towards North Korea, with President Asif Ali Zardari and the Foreign Office extending greetings to Pyongyang on the 78th anniversary of the country’s founding.
In a letter to DPRK President Kim Jong Un on the 78th founding anniversary of the republic, President Zardari referred to the two countries’ “cordial relations based on mutual trust and goodwill” and expressed the hope that bilateral ties would continue to grow in the interests of both countries.
